identity.title: A lactylation-associated transcriptomic signature predicts outcome and identifies CBX3 dependency in multiple myeloma.

content.abstract: Lactate accumulation is associated with the progression of multiple myeloma (MM) and resistance to treatment, but the clinical implications of lactylation-associated transcription in MM are not yet fully understood. We integrated public transcriptomic, metabolomic, proteomic, and genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening data to examine this relationship. A transcriptomic score derived from a curated set of 398 lactylation-associated genes increased across disease stages and adverse clinical groups. Six genes (CBX3, DDX21, GAPDH, HNRNPC, ILF2, and NUP133) associated with overall survival across four cohorts were retained as a fixed candidate panel. In the CoMMpass development cohort, a multivariable Cox model based on standardized expression yielded an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.648 (95% CI, 0.605-0.693). The continuous six-gene score remained associated with overall survival in the three replication cohorts (hazard ratios per standard-deviation increase, 1.33-1.58). Genome-wide CRISPR screening identified CBX3 as an MM-cell dependency. CBX3 knockout reduced cell proliferation and global lysine lactylation, whereas inhibition of lactate production reduced CBX3 protein abundance. These findings clarify the relationship between lactylation-associated transcription and MM pathophysiology.
